accepted.evidence: Dhakal p. 60 prints /kʰəs.rə/ “rough.” Turner3855 section 2 gives Nepali khasro “rough, coarse, thick” under *khasara-. The Darai s-r sequence and sense select section 2; section 1 has shorter khas- forms.
Dhakal p. 61 prints /cin.ta/ “worry.” Turner4816 gives Old Gujarati cīṁta “worry,” with Pali cintā and Prakrit ciṁtā “thought, care”; form and sense are direct matches.

held.reason: Dhakal p. 60 gives “trust” and Turner11966 viśvāsa has the same sense, but Darai bisvas appears learned relative to Turner’s vernacular bisās; immediate Nepali/learned transmission is unresolved.
Dhakal p. 60 gives “husband’s younger sister,” corresponding semantically to Turner6946 nánāndr̥ and Nepali nanda, but the Darai m-d cluster has no demonstrated sound development.
Dhakal p. 61 gives “message,” but searches for samācāra and the Darai shape found no precise Turner article or branch.
